newsitem.title: USA: Exxon, Ashland profits soar on high refining margins. [CORRECTED 23:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Exxon, Ashland profits soar on high refining margins. [CORRECTED 23:05 GMT]

text.p: Exxon Corp. said Monday its profits surged 25 percent in the second quarter, as higher margins in its refining and chemicals businesses pushed earnings beyond the most optimistic Wall Street forecasts.
Exxon's net income totalled $1.97 billion in the second quarter, up from $1.57 billion in the same year-ago period. Earnings per share rose to 79 cents from 63 cents a year ago.
Exxon said revenues rose to $32.7 billion in the quarter vs. $32.3 billion a year ago.

"Earnings benefited from generally stronger downstream margins and higher petroleum product sales," Exxon Chairman Lee Raymond said in a statement. "Chemicals volumes and margins also improved over the prior year's quarter."
The results easily surpassed analysts' expectations of 72 cents a share, according to estimates compiled by First Call, and even beat the high-end forecast of 75 cents.

"We anticipated that lower crude oil prices would bolster refining margins, but this figure is much stronger than we had thought and the improvement was global," said Michael Young, at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, who had been at the top of the range of analysts' estimates.

U.S. refining and marketing operations earnings rose to $162 million from $98 million, boosted by a strong performance on the U.S. Gulf Coast, the company said. Most analysts had been predicting a flat performance year-on-year.
Overseas refining and marketing earnings nearly tripled, climbing to $382 million in the second quarter from $134 million a year ago.
Sales of oil products such as gasoline and heating oil climbed nearly 6 percent, to 5.4 million barrels per day, the highest in 20 years.
Profits for the oil giant's chemicals business rose 29 percent over last year to $393 million.

Exxon said second-quarter exploration and production earnings were hurt by lower year-on-year crude oil prices. Crude oil prices in the second quarter averaged $1.50 per barrel below last year's levels, the company said.
Net income on U.S. operations fell to $335 million, from $423 million in last year's second quarter, while overseas profits edged up to $620 million, from $615 million.
For the first six months of 1996, net income totalled $4.1 billion, compared with $3.5 billion in last year's first half.
Exxon stock rose 87.5 cents to $61.31 in consolidated New York Stock Exchange midafternoon trading.
Strong refining margins also helped boost earnings at Ashland Inc., helping the Kentucky-based (corrects from Texas-based) oil refiner post its best-ever quarterly performance.
Ashland's net income climbed 58 percent to a record $126 million, or $1.66 a share, for the company's fiscal third quarter, compared with $80 million, or $1.16 a share, a year ago.
The results beat analysts' average forecast of $1.34 a share, according to First Call.
Revenues rose to $3.5 billion for the quarter from $3.4 billion a year ago.

Behind the strong performance was a sharp increase in operating income from the company's refining and marketing unit. Refining operating income jumped to $96 million in the second quarter from $53 million in the same year-ago period.
Ashland said its refining margins rose $1.18 per barrel, reflecting lower crude oil costs on the year.
Ashland stock rose $1.19 to $49 in consolidated midafternoon NYSE trading.
